steps.what: Select study statistics and specify charts, denominators, geography and reporting period
Assemble statistics, charts and graphs into the report layout
Explain study findings and verify the completed report and illustrations

tasks.design: Configure linked tables and chart layouts in {DOCS} using the planner's checked {SPREADSHEET} table and specification. The planner explains results and checks scales, comparisons and caveats before accepting the report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated chart formatting and copying separated the report from its selected figures.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked charts and report templates can reuse a specified table without interpreting the study.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing valid comparisons and explaining uncertainty remain planning work.
tasks.human_edge: The planner decides what the results mean for the place and its residents.
tasks.altitude: Less report assembly; the planner retains the same analytical and publication authority.

reach.task: Document denominators and uncertainty in study tables

evidence.claim: Linked tables and reusable chart layouts can reduce repeated report assembly; the proposed hours are unmeasured task scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is communicating completed study results, excluding field collection, analytical model construction, map database maintenance and public publication; allocate each action once across tasks.

Planner produces the checked reporting table and specification in s1: study version, geography, period, measure, value, unit, denominator, missing-value treatment, chart type, axis limits, labels and source references. Selection and capture consume all 30 hours; no structured chart choice is assumed free.

Existing study analysts produce the underlying results through unchanged research outside this report task; the planner checks their suitability in s1. Unsupported schemas or chart types return to manual assembly within s3; unusually difficult cases lose the proposed saving.
Try native linked charts and templates first. s3 includes checking generated labels and every represented comparison; no generated narrative or automatic statistical interpretation is proposed.
unknowns: How often study tables repeat a compatible structure
Whether native chart links survive document conversion
research_questions: How much assembly time remains after checking axes and denominators on five previous reports?

already_counted.description: Capture reporting fields, interpret findings and check illustrations including manual exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain chart layouts and field mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed report version, linked table snapshot, charts and caveats; any edit voids acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net=18. Range assumes only some repeat studies use the layout and bespoke charts require manual reconstruction; no collection or analytical time is saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose map layers and specify database changes, coordinate systems and matching rules
Load selected layers and update matching map database records in geographic information software
Maintain maps and databases after checking geographic alignment and resolving exceptions

tasks.design: Configure staged imports and fixed matching rules in {OTHER}, the geographic information system. The planner chooses the authoritative layers, checks spatial meaning and accepts each database revision after resolving exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring layer updates involved repeated field mapping and manual record loading.
tasks.enabler_now: Geographic information systems support saved import definitions, staging and repeatable coordinate transformations.
tasks.still_hard: A technically valid layer can describe the wrong date, area or planning concept.
tasks.human_edge: The planner judges source relevance and the consequences of conflicting boundaries.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive loading; ownership of map interpretation and revisions stays with the planner.

reach.task: Validate spatial registration of updated layers
reach.learn: Coordinate reference systems and spatial quality checks

evidence.claim: Saved geographic data imports can repeat explicit mappings and transformations; these labour estimates are model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is maintaining persistent planning layers and their database, excluding study-specific field compilation, report charts and administrative file archiving; shared actions must have one owner.

OTHER means geographic information software. Existing mapping authorities or survey teams produce source layers through unchanged work: feature identifier, geometry, coordinate reference system, source version, effective date and attributes with units. Availability in this form is a customer condition, not an assumed free conversion service.

Planner checks and captures layer version, target fields, identifiers, coordinate system, units, update extent, duplicate rule and transformation in s1's 35 hours. Missing source metadata or incompatible layers stop the import and return to manual reconstruction and checking in s3; no inferred zoning status is written.

Use native import configuration before custom code. s3's 40 hours include checking alignment against source features, attributes, deletions, temporal validity and manual exceptions; no benefit is credited for system runtime.
unknowns: Whether authoritative layers carry stable identifiers and coordinate metadata
How much existing load time is repetitive rather than corrective
research_questions: Do staged updates reproduce current maps without moving features or changing attribute meaning?

already_counted.description: Specify source mappings and check spatial revisions including manual exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain import mappings and retest layer schema changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact staged revision with source layer versions, transformations, resolved exceptions and spatial checks; any change voids acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25; subtract 8 focal upkeep for central net=17. Range assumes several layers need manual repair and only recurring compatible updates avoid loading effort; no field survey or GIS runtime saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep land use files and records current

steps.what: Select records for filing and capture land use metadata and version relationships
Copy files and statistics into parallel folders and tracking lists
Verify retrieval, correct filing errors and maintain the accepted record version

tasks.design: Keep one versioned record in {DOCS}, with saved views replacing duplicate folders and a separate {SPREADSHEET} index. The planner captures metadata and checks retrieval and version links in the existing record store.
tasks.previous_blocker: Copies and parallel indexes obscured which land use record was current.
tasks.enabler_now: Native metadata, links and version history can serve several views of the same record.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what belongs in the record and when a new version supersedes an old one.
tasks.human_edge: The planner understands the provenance and limits of land use statistics.
tasks.altitude: Fewer duplicate filing operations; record selection and responsibility stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: A single versioned document record with metadata views can replace parallel filing copies where these exist; the time scenario is unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary is administrative record maintenance, not creating statistical results, updating map features or writing planning reports. A customer without parallel filing has no s2 saving.

Planner produces the filing manifest in s1: record identifier, source, source version, geography, reporting period, record type, superseded record identifier and destination access group. All selection, metadata capture and checking remain in the 35 hours; no classifier supplies these for free.

Study authors produce original records through unchanged study work. Eliminating s2 consumes only s1's checked metadata and existing files; s3 retains filing and retrieval effort. Incomplete metadata or access conflicts are corrected manually in s3 before acceptance.

Try native document views and versioning first. Initial migration is in build time; ongoing index maintenance and exceptional filing remain in s3 with additional upkeep below. Retention and access rules require customer confirmation.
unknowns: Whether duplicate filing accounts for the stated baseline share
Whether required record views can use links instead of copies
research_questions: Can users retrieve each sample record and its superseded version from one store without a parallel index?

already_counted.description: Capture metadata and verify versions, retrieval and exceptional filing

incremental.description: Maintain document views and check broken version links

approvals.approved_version: Exact record index version, source record versions, supersession links and access groups; changes require a new check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65, gross=35; minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net=28. Range assumes only part of parallel filing is removable because some records require separate controlled copies; no creation or metadata capture time disappears.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Research relevant maps, reports, investigations and books and record source passages
Compile and organize selected passages by project question

loop.purpose: Suggest an organization of selected textual evidence
loop.input: Planner-selected source passages and explicit project questions
loop.output: Draft grouped passages with source locators and unresolved contradictions
loop.check: Planner checks every grouping against the original passage, context and question; checks omitted contrary evidence
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; uncertain groups return to manual organization in this step
loop.why_not_simpler: Headings can be fixed but relevance of differently worded passages requires reading; native folders remain the fallback

steps.what: Analyze information, reconcile conflicting sources and determine its use in the project

tasks.design: Use native folders and reference links in {DOCS} first, with a bounded loop only to suggest thematic grouping of selected passages. The planner verifies each grouping and retains all source research, spatial interpretation and analytical conclusions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant evidence used different terminology across reports and investigations.
tasks.enabler_now: Text tools can suggest thematic groupings, while source locators permit direct checking.
tasks.still_hard: Source reliability, contradictory evidence and spatial context cannot be established from a tidy outline.
tasks.human_edge: The planner decides which evidence bears on the real project and why.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in organizing excerpts; research and judgement remain the main work.

reach.task: Code textual evidence against research questions
reach.learn: Source context and checks for omitted contrary material

evidence.claim: MAXQDA suggests qualitative codes and advises checking every AI-coded segment; this supports assisted thematic organization rather than automatic planning conclusions.
The bounded organization loop and proposed small net saving are unmeasured model scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary is cross-source research synthesis for a particular project, excluding record archiving, map database updates, report layout and single environmental-report passage retrieval already owned by other tasks; count repeated actions once.

Planner creates the research brief and selected bundle in s1's 45 hours: question identifiers, selected source identifiers, versions, page or section locators, exact excerpts and unresolved research questions. Capture and verification are counted; the model supplies no authoritative relevance flag.

Source authors produce the original materials through unchanged external work. Unreadable passages, maps or unavailable source text stay manual; no image-to-map inference is proposed. s2 includes checking and manual exceptions in its retained 13 hours.

Try native reference organization first and omit the loop if it adds no benefit. Maps and books still require direct human reading; confidential source access and applicable national rules need customer review.
unknowns: Whether source material can be processed with adequate confidentiality
Whether grouping saves more time than checking it
research_questions: Does assisted grouping reduce effort while preserving contradictory passages in a small project sample?

already_counted.description: Check suggested thematic groupings and manually handle uncertain passages

incremental.description: Maintain grouping instructions and audit omission patterns

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=93, gross=7; subtract 5 focal upkeep for central net=2. Range assumes much source material remains manual and most drafting gains are consumed by context and omission checks; no research or analysis saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The planner spends less time copying and formatting repeat material, with unchanged responsibility for planning evidence and decisions.
reach: Learn spatial quality checks with remote sensing technicians
Learn source coding and reproducibility with social science research assistants
skills_to_grow: Specify reproducible charts and layer imports
role.ambitious_version: Produce clearer, traceable planning evidence while retaining human responsibility for interpretation and choices.
